The results have been better (winning back-to-back games against two of their divisional foes), but the process of how the Texans have been staying in, and now winning, football games has taken on a different shape than anticipated. The Texans’ defense has been more or less average this season. They’ve faced a litany of top-end quarterbacks, a byproduct of life in the AFC, and the yielding of big plays by their young and talented defensive back room has included a surprisingly large number moments of losing in contested-catch situations. Even when performing well down-to-down, like holding Joe Burrow to his second-lowest success rate in a game in his career in their week 2 matchup against the Bengals, Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter just couldn’t make plays when it mattered the most. Add on linebacker injuries, and the defense that many anticipated to be a true needle-moving unit felt much more mortal through the first month of the season. Will Anderson Jr. is still playing like a star and the deserved frontrunner for Defensive Player of the Year, but offenses and top-end quarterbacks were still finding answers against a defense that’s usually suffocating. On the offensive side of the ball, perhaps more predictably, the Texans’ run game has continued to be lackluster. The unit ranks 25th in rushing success rate on running back runs, with a whopping 29.4% of their running back runs going for a successful gain on early downs. And that ranking is actually an improvement over where the Texans’ run game was the first three seasons of Stroud’s career, where they ranked 31st. The Texans still face plenty of third and longs this season, averaging 7.1 yards on third down, but again, it’s still an improvement over their 7.4 average over the previous three seasons, which ranked 30th over that time period (7.1 ranks 17th, which isn’t bad when you were at the bottom of the barrel before!). What’s behind Houston’s passing surge? What is different this year in Houston is the aerial assault that feels more like the Run N’ Shoot days when Warren Moon was playing with the Oilers. The Texans are chucking it in Nick Caley’s second season as offensive coordinator, ranking 26th in designed run rate on early downs this season, with their designed run rate dropping from 45.9% from 2023-2025, which ranked 14th, to 37% this year. The Texans are using condensed formations at a 40.2% rate this season, per NextGenStats, a drop from 49.6% last year and a far cry from 2024 when the Texans used condensed formations at a 56.6% rate in Bobby Slowik’s last season as offensive coordinator. It’s more than just formation usage and leaning into the pass. Stroud has been simply excelling with a more spaced-out offense that lets him quickly diagnose defenses. Caley is asking Stroud to constantly drop back, be right, and to find the correct answers, and Stroud is happily obliging. Stroud currently ranks fifth in dropback success rate this season and sixth in explosive pass rate. He is operating quickly and pushing the ball over and over to his pass-catchers. Stroud ranks first in the NFL in passes between the numbers and first in air yards relative to the sticks (i.e. how far in front or past the first down marker the quarterback is throwing.) Stroud’s average air yards to the sticks mark is at 1.2, over a yard higher than his career average of -0.2, and even higher than the league average this season of -0.6. If you just look success rate on passes thrown, so removing sacks and scrambles, Stroud ranks second this season, behind only Jared Goff. He’s basically filled in the area between the hashes with dots on his target chart this season. C.J. Stroud's target chart for the 2026 season. (TruMedia) Stroud isn’t just aimlessly chucking throws down the field. He has been aggressive but methodical and making quick decisions. These big throws down the field aren’t with play-action guardrails and in a paint-by-numbers scheme. Stroud is asked to dropback and find his answer over and over again, and when he gets to do so, his numbers still stay among the league’s best. Even with the Texans’ iffy offensive line, Stroud has been hit or sacked on only 11.4% of his dropbacks this season, a mark that ranks third in the NFL. He hasn’t taken a single sack this year against the blitz and ranks first in SUPLEX (success rate plus explosive play rate) among all NFL quarterbacks against the blitz while also getting hit or sacked at the lowest rate as well. I highlight Stroud’s play against the blitz because that’s where you can really see how quickly Stroud is seeing the game right now. He is not surprised when he is hot (meaning when there is an unblocked pass rusher) and has been finding answer after answer. here's a couple from last week against the Titans. Foster Moreau is left wide open and the @HoustonTexans are on the board. item.title: Boonsboro shuts out Clear Spring in flag football region semifinals
item.description: The MPSSAA flag football playoffs continued with the start of region semifinals on Thursday, Oct. 22, with a trio of Washington County tams in action. Here's what happened: 2A-1A West I semifinals Boonsboro 30, Clear Spring 0 Mylee Hartman threw for two touchdowns and rushed for two more, and McKenna Johnson had a TD catch and a long pick-six as the No. 2-seed Warriors (8-2) pulled away from the No. 3 Blazers (5-6). Hartman's 1-yard TD run gave Boonsboro -- the reigning three-time county champions -- a 6-0 lead in the first quarter. The Blazers drove inside the Warriors 10-yard line, but Hartman intercepted a Clear Spring pass at the goal line on fourth down, stopping the Blazers' best scoring chance of the game. Hartman's 10-yard TD strike to Johnson doubled the lead in the second quarter, and Boonsboro made a fourth-down stop on a Brennyn Cronise sack with Clear Spring in Warriors territory to keep the score 12-0 into halftime. The Blazers marched into the red zone again in the third quarter, but Johnson jumped a pass and took an interception 68 yards untouched up the right sideline to make it 18-0. That was the first of Johnson's two interceptions in the contest. In the fourth quarter, Hartman added a 35-yard TD pass to Harmony Redding and a 9-yard scoring run. Boonsboro will either travel to No. 1 Smithsburg or host No. 4 Williamsport for the region final on Oct. 27 or 28. The Leopards host the Wildcats in a semifinal on Oct. 24 at 11 a.m. 4A-3A West I semifinals Urbana 43, South Hagerstown 0 The No. 1-seed Hawks (11-0) rolled past the No. 4 Rebels (0-9). Wednesday, Oct. 21 3A-2A West I quarterfinals Tuscarora 31, North Hagerstown 0 The No. 4-seed Titans (4-7), playing at home, shut out the No. 5 Hubs (3-9). item.title: Purdue basketball's second half surge carries Boilers past Purdue Fort Wayne
item.description: FORT WAYNE − Purdue basketball found its first road trip of the season to possess a tougher challenge than its first exhibition game. Ultimately, the Boilermakers had enough firepower to topple Purdue Fort Wayne 93-62 at Memorial Coliseum. Purdue used a late first half surge and a dominant second half to pull away from the Mastodons. Along the way, the Boilers shot 58.1%, including going 13-for-33 from 3-point range. Purdue basketball turning point vs. Purdue Fort Wayne Purdue was marred by a few ugly 3-point shots and three early turnovers in a game that was tied at 19 past the midway point of the first half. Back-to-back 3s by CJ Cox and Omer Mayer followed a pair of Daniel Jacobsen free throws. The Boilermakers outscored Fort Wayne 23-12 over the final 7:06 of the first half and led 42-31 at halftime. Purdue was mostly on cruise control from there. More: Purdue basketball can't pinpoint potential leading scorer, but Antione West can Game MVP There is no definitive alpha leader on this team. But it feels like this is CJ Cox's team. The third-year starter has owned that through two exhibition games. After scoring 15 points and making 5 of 6 3-pointers against Ball State last Sunday, Cox's shot making again lifted the Boilermakers. Cox made 6 of 9 field goals and scored 13 points to go with 4 rebounds and 2 assists in 21 minutes. Through two exhibition games, Cox is shooting 64.7% and averaging 14 points in 37 total minutes. 3 more stars for Purdue basketball vs. Purdue Fort Wayne Antione West: At one point, West made three straight 3-point attempts. His banked 3-pointer got Purdue out of a funk where it had five empty possessions on its previous six trips on offense. West finished with 16 points, 3 rebounds and a steal. Jack Benter: Coach Matt Painter acknowledged Benter's assists-to-turnover ration (14-to-1) in competitive practice drills. What Painter didn't mention was Benter's rebounding. The redshirt sophomore put that on display Thursday. Benter finished with 10 boards to go with Omer Mayer: After four years of watching a table setter play point guard in Braden Smith, Purdue is getting treated to a score-first mentality at the position. Mayer scored 15 points to go with 4 assists, 2 rebounds and 2 steals. Sam King covers sports for the Journal & Courier. Email him at sking@jconline.com and follow him on X and Instagram @samueltking. item.title: Ex-Dodgers pitcher Dustin May gets brutally honest on reaching World Series with Brewers
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Ex-Dodgers pitcher Dustin May gets brutally honest on reaching World Series with Brewers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There was a time when Dustin May was considered to be a future star with the Los Angeles Dodgers. He displayed promise with LA from 2019-2025, but injuries impacted his career along the way. He’s since pitched for the Boston Red Sox, St. Louis Cardinals and now the Milwaukee Brewers . May joined the Brewers earlier this season and is now set to pitch in the World Series with Milwaukee. Prior to this year, May hadn’t pitched in the postseason since LA’s 2020 World Series run. He got brutally honest on his journey during an interview on Thursday, via Foul Territory. “Very blessed to be here,” May said. “I thank the Lord everyday for just giving me the opportunity to be here. Looking back over the last two years, I mean, two years ago I wasn’t sure if I was ever going to play again. So being able to be here, be on this stage again, with this team, in this moment, I’m very lucky and blessed.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) May was acquired by the Brewers from the Cardinals before the trade deadline this season. He did not pitch especially well with Milwaukee, turning in a 5.65 ERA across 10 starts. He’s made three appearances (one start) so far in the postseason, pitching to a 6.43 ERA. His numbers are not ideal, but May is a veteran pitcher who can make an impact either in a starting or bullpen role. It would not be surprising to see him end up having a crucial multi-inning relief appearance in the Fall Classic at some point. Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur doesn’t seem to be too concerned about the status of his team’s top two weapons downfield heading into Sunday’s game at Ford Field against the Detroit Lions. Asked whether he was worried about wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden not playing against the Lions, LaFleur simply said “No,” according to Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Both Watson and Golden haven’t practiced fully this week, but nothing seems serious enough to worry about for the two talented wide receivers. Watson is leading the team with 538 receiving yards, six touchdowns and 20 first downs on 29 receptions and 57 targets. Golden, on the other hand, is in the middle of what is becoming his breakout season in the pros. He is second on the team with 501 receiving yards, three scores, and 23 first downs on 30 catches and 57 targets. Thanks in large part to those two playmakers downfield, Green Bay has become one of the most prolific passing teams in the league to date. Jordan Love is leading the Packers’ attack that is averaging 269.3 passing yards per game — fifth best overall in the NFL. Green Bay is looking to sustain its momentum as it tries to catch the Minnesota Vikings atop the NFC North Division standings. The Packers, who lost to the Vikings in Week 1 and to the Atlanta Falcons in Week 3, carry a 4-2 record to the Lions game. They are also on a three-game winning streak after beating the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field in Green Bay in Week 6. Not only is the record bad, but they don’t even do very many things particularly well. Special teams has the crown of boasting the team’s best individual player— Chase McLaughlin. There is no better Tampa bay Buccaneer at this point in time than McLaughlin, however, on the other side of things they have a highly inconsistent, unreliable, well-paid punter. With an underratedly-formidable opponent on the schedule this week, the Buccaneers don’t have a significantly clear path to victory. Tampa is the underdog, should be the underdog, and will need to play above their skis just to hang around and maybe pull out a close victory. The issue, even in that game theory, is the Buccaneers have been absolutely horrendous in close games. Every week the Buccaneers seem to find themselves in one-score games and they manifest ways to lose them. Tampa has been in 1-5 in one-score games this season— That’s bad, but it gets worse. The Buccaneers have been 3-9 in last 12 one-score games. Worse still, the team’s record in games that have been decided by one score, under Todd Bowles is an appalling 19-24. So it would seem their best path to victory would be blowing out the Carolina Panthers, and somehow that seems even more unlikely. Can the Buccaneers win? I mean it’s just like you put all the offensive players in one bag and I just take a baseball bat and beat on the bag.” Deacon Jones How can the Buccaneers lose? Fail to slow down Bryce Young. Simply put, Bryce Young has been sensational this season. In 2026, national media will treat the Carolina Panthers and the entire NFC South like speed limits on the I-95. While being ignored, Young has produced. The Panthers are only 3-2 (not great, but by the standards of the NFC South— Superb), however, Young has been lights out. Carolina’s former number one overall pick, turned bust, has now transformed himself into a very good player. In five games, Young’s thrown 11 touchdowns to go along with only two interceptions. Those are numbers that weren’t even in the range of reachable for Young based on his performance over the last few seasons, but we are here not there. Carolina’s offense has totaled 25+ points in all but one game this season, they average the fourth most points per game in the league. The Buccaneers’ defense has been fluky in 2026. The group has been really reliable and able to stall offenses of both high and low caliber, until the team really needs them to. At that point, they tend to fold. Statistically, the matchup should be a good one. The Buccaneers have the defense to combat Carolina’s attack and favor may even be on the Bucs’ side as Bryce Young has been pretty consistently sacked this season— 12 times in just five games which plays right into what has been a weakness for Todd Bowles’ defense for nearly a half-decade now. Sunday would be an excellent opportunity for guys like Yaya Diaby and Calijah to Kancey to start their season and also for Rueben Bain Jr. and David Walker to continue to build on their momentum from a week ago— three sacks between the two of them. In 2026, Young and the Panthers are an opponent that needs to be respected. They are in first place and will be motivated to stay there. For the better part of the 2020’s, the NFC South has been victim to tiebreakers— Divisional games matter and there is a zero percent the Panthers will be overlooking the Buccaneers on Sunday.

Super lightweight Dalton Smith pulled off an impressive upset win to start 2026. He did something no other opponent had done, stopping the relentless power puncher Subriel Matias of Puerto Rico in five rounds to become the new WBC World Super Lightweight champion. Smith won by coming straight at Matias to neutralize his pressure head-on, instead of boxing and playing it safe. It paid off. Dalton vs Puello heads a Machroom Boxing card featuring a grudge match between top women’s super flyweights Shannon Ryan and Emma Dolan, the return of veteran Maxi Hughes, and an appearance by exciting young heavyweight Leo Atang. The fight card airs on DAZN Boxing in the U.S. starting with prelims at 12 noon ET/9 a.m. PT , and the main card at 2 p.m. ET/11 a.m. PT. Super lightweight Dalton Smith pulled off an impressive upset win to start 2026. He did something no other opponent had done, stopping the relentless power puncher Subriel Matias of Puerto Rico in five rounds to become the new WBC World Super Lightweight champion. Smith won by coming straight at Matias to neutralize his pressure head-on, instead of boxing and playing it safe. It paid off. Now Smith returns to face the man who lost that same belt to Matias six months earlier, Alberto Puello of the Dominican Republic based in Las Vegas (25-1, 11 KOs). Puello wants his title back, and he’s highly motivated to beat Smith. Both men know a win puts they close to a potential unification fight in the division. Now that Shakur Stevenson is no longer working with Zuffa Boxing, he becomes a realistic option, which only adds to the motivation of both men. Matchroom Boxing promoter Eddie Hearn called it an important night for Smith. Hearn has made no secret of his wish to stage a stadium fight or major unification bout for Smith, potentially next spring at Sheffield’s Hillsborough Stadium. But first, Smith needs to take care of his business on Saturday. Smith, Puello and several undercard fighters had their say at the final pre-fight news conference in Sheffield on Thursday. Dalton Smith: “There Are No Easy Fights” Smith, who generally prefers to do his talking in the ring, said he’s well aware of the challenge ahead, but added that he’s never avoided a fight. “I have always fought who I have needed to fight in front of me. And I have always come out victorious,” said Smith. Smith said his big win in Brooklyn in January is now old news, and he intends to pick up right where he left off after stopping Subriel Matias. “The best fighters bring the best out of me. That’s why on Saturday night you are going to get the best version of Dalton Smith.” Smith said he’s watched Alberto Puello for well over a year, including the controversial majority decision loss by Puello to Matias, which he watched ringside last summer. “I go into this fight feeling very confident. I have prepared for this like I am the challenger and on Saturday night I will prove to the boxing world why I am number one. “I am cool, calm, collected, and I will do it again on Saturday. It’s massive, and without the support that I’ve got, I wouldn’t be able to do this. I’ve got one of the best teams around and Saturday night is going to be special, and the atmosphere is going to be electric,” promised Smith. Alberto Puello: “We Are Here For A War” Alberto Puello handed Gary Antuanne Russell his only loss. Can he do the same to Dalton Smith on Saturday? Photo: Esther Lin, Premier Boxing Champions Puello admits the loss to Matias was difficult for him to accept. The margins were razor thin, and a significant number of observers believed Matias had won, including this writer. Puello intends to get revenge by taking the belt back from its current owner, Dalton Smith. “Now we are here for a war. I am here to get back that title that was taken away from me. We come in now better prepared for the fight than we were last time against Subriel Matias and we are ready to get back what is ours,” said Puello. Puello wouldn’t give up any details about his game plan. “I say that I am a level above him because I believe that I have faced a level of opponents who are above him during my career. Of course, that is in spite of the fact that he has beaten one of the opponents who beat me,” adding that he still believes he won against Matias. Dalton Smith and Alberto Puello promise an action fight on Saturday. Photo: Mark Robinson, Matchroom Boxing Puello still has plenty of gas in the tank at age 32, but he’s a steady grinder rather than a knockout puncher. Smith had dropped his last six opponents, and stopped all but one of them. He has put together a 74% knockout rate with little fanfare. No one should be surprised anymore to see Smith take out on an opponent. Puello has never been stopped. If Smith can do it, it would be a significant accomplishment and give him leverage to set up a unification fight in the first half of 2027, possibly against Stevenson. Undercard Matchups from Sheffield Several undercard fights are worth your attention. British super flyweight rivals Shannon Ryan (11-1, 2 KOs) and Emma Dolan of Nottingham (9-1, 1 KO) will meet in a rematch of Dolan’s upset win over Ryan in June 2024. Since then, Dolan lost her bid for the IBF World Super Flyweight title in April against Irma Garcia of Mexico, but has bounced back with a decision win. After Ryan lost the British and Commonwealth titles to Dolan, she’s been on a winning streak with four victories, two by knockout, winning back the Commonwealth title. Now the British title in Dolan’s hands will also be on the line. “ I need to right that wrong in order to move on and fight for the world championship,” said Ryan, who is ranked number one and in line to be the IBF mandatory challenger to Irma Garcia.. “Yes, I am number one. But for me to really feel and know that I am number one, I simply have to right this wrong and then push on for what is next.” Ryan says she’s a different person than the woman who lost to Dolan. “I think everyone can see that my boxing has improved tremendously since then, too. I’ll be bringing the same aggression, the same chaos. But I am a better boxer. As long as I listen to my team, I believe that I can win this fight in any way I want it to go. I can get the win by any means.” Dolan is delighted to have the rematch on British soil on a British championship card. “I feel really, really good, I’ve had a great camp and I’m looking forward to making it 2-0. I feel like I have improved a lot and I am definitely a better version of myself going into this fight,” said Dolan. Can Maxi Hughes repeat his upset win over Gary Cully on Saturday against another undefeated prospect in Georgio Visioli? Photo: Mark Robinson, Matchroom Boxing Veteran and fan favorite Maxi Hughes isn’t quite done with boxing. The 36-year-old from Yorkshire (29-9-2, 6 KOs) will test lightweight prospect Giorgio Visioli of Hampshire (11-0, 6 KOs). Hughes says you can call him the “Matchroom Exterminator.” He defeated Kid Galahad and Gary Cully, both considered rising talents. Joking with promoter Eddie Hearn , Hughes said, “I’m not sure what Giorgio has done to upset you, but maybe you’ve brought me here to get rid of him.” Hughes said he feels good after a full camp and not fighting on short notice. Hughes says the pressure is all on Visioli. “I am his biggest fight. I expect nothing less. We’ll see if he’s got it in him when the bell goes, under the lights, against someone like myself, because I’ve been there and done it around the world, against many different styles. I have the experience and I’ve done it the hard way, most of the time in the away corner.” Visioli confirmed that Hughes was the first name offered to him, and he said yes without hesitation. “You might call it ego, but it’s not ego. You’re allowed self-belief in this sport, but I think some people don’t like that. If I believe in myself, then I’ll take the opportunity. “But for me to push on in my career then I think the stoppage is there. It’s a must do and that is what I am going to do.” Also on the card, bright young heavyweight Leo Atang of Yorkshire (9-0, 8 KOs) will face Jonathan Exequiel

item.title: ‘They might be finished already’: Eddie Hearn says Zuffa Boxing collapsing
item.description: Matchroom’s Eddie Hearn can help but grin while taking at least some pleasure in Zuffa Boxing struggling as of late, and watching Dana White squirm under the pressure. Check out some of what he had to say as he believes we may in fact be in the end days of Zuffa Boxing as a relevant company in this business. Hearn on Dana White’s recent struggles in the boxing business “I said when these guys come into boxing, ‘you are not going to enjoy this.’ Because when you’ve operated like those guys have, with total control and the ability to mute media, to do what you want and just to have people say yes — boxing is so much different. You’re not going to get your own way, you’re going to get faced with criticism, the media ask much tougher questions, and you will not enjoy it. “Well, that’s the understatement of the year because they have had an absolute disaster, Zuffa. They’ve had the worst start they could ever have in the sport. The UFC business is in terrible decline. Even the ratings for WWE are down. But also, you can see how it’s affecting Dana. He’s forgetting things, he’s getting flustered. And I know I joke about the blood pressure and the capillaries, but it’s for real. “I don’t want to sound facetious but I’ve almost go to the point where I feel sorry for him now…It’s just done. It’s over. So, I think Zuffa Boxing, I think they might be finished already. They have not done a show in America since July. It’s November next week. They’ve done one show in the UK which, let’s be honest, I don’t mean to be disrespectful, was awful. They’ve got another one coming up which is bang average. Ben Shalom’s shows are 5x better, 10x better than Zuffa shows. “So, what are they going to do? For a six month period they are not doing one show in America, and they’re doing two bang average shows in the UK. These guys don’t know what they’re doing. I think they’re done. Everyone’s gone quiet. Shakur Stevenson’s left before he’s even had a fight — that’s a PR disaster. “I expected these guys to be better at what they do. But I didn’t expect it to affect them so badly and for it to start — you can see the physical breakdown, the mental and emotional breakdown of what is happening when [Dana’s] up there [at the press conferences]. You can see it’s like affecting him. And this is a horrible, horrible business. That’s why I feel almost bad for those guys because I know what it’s like. You have to become really battle worn to it…I was expecting a real fight [out of them], but I think they’re done.”

The trade itself should not have come as too much of a surprise, as he was one year away from free agency, and the Brewers had done the same with Corbin Burnes, Devin Williams and Josh Hader. Peralta struggled with the Mets, and the Brewers looked like geniuses for dealing him. However, the Tampa Bay Rays went and got him from the Mets at the trade deadline, and he turned things around. Peralta went from looking like a player who was going to need to sign a prove-it style deal to someone who now seems poised to get paid handsomely. Peralta spoke to reporters on Thursday and made it clear that he wants to stay in Tampa Bay. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! "I'm very comfortable here, and I would love to stay here for the rest of my career," Peralta told "Foul Territory." "There are a lot of people that I love here, and a lot of people that care about each other. I think they're very smart. They know what they are doing." Peralta noted that he thinks the Rays will help him get even better, and the fact that he already lives in Florida. The only problem is that he seems poised for a nine-figure deal, and the Rays are not a team that typically gives out that kind of money. Peralta won the American League Championship Series MVP Award and has been very important to this run by the Rays. item.description: Is A.J. Brown playing tonight? Why Patriots WR is off to slow start in Week 7 originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A.J. Brown's first season with the New England Patriots has not gone according to plan. Brown had a quiet Week 1 and suffered a high-ankle sprain in the same game that forced him to miss a handful of contests after that. Then, in his return in Week 6, Brown once again had a disappointing performance that included some ugly drops. In Week 7 against the Chicago Bears , Brown is off to a slow start yet again for New England. Here's a closer look at what's going on. Is A.J. Brown playing tonight? Yes, Brown is playing on Thursday night, he just hasn't been able to reel in a catch yet. He does have one target, though. The Patriots' offense has not been crisp through two drives, with the unit getting just one first down, so Brown hasn't exactly had a chance to get going. Drake Maye has connected on a few passes, but all three have gone to running backs Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. Hopefully the third drive and beyond will yield better results. item.title: Saints and Steelers Vying for Title of 'France's Team' in Paris Game
item.description: The New Orleans Saints are heading to France to play a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. It's the story of the week in the New Orleans sports market. Many things in Louisiana, including the name of the state, named after King Louis, have French ties. The name of the Saints' city is New Orleans, named after Orleans, France. Orleans is located an hour and a half south of Paris depending on your mode of travel. The Saints will be playing close enough for Saints fans going on the road to travel there, too. The Associated Press' Ken Maguire discussed the origins of New Orleans' name and the Saints' logo. Here's some of what Maguire had to write on the topic. "As the NFL has expanded globally — this season there are a record nine international games — the league has allowed teams to claim countries in its “global markets” program. The Saints are currently the only team with marketing rights in France. The designation lets them sign commercial deals and grow their fan base in the country. 'They’re in good position. They’re becoming France’s team, which is great,' said Brett Gosper, the NFL’s head of Europe and Asia-Pacific. 'I don’t think it will be long before other teams turn up in France, because it’s such a great market,' he added. 'The Saints may enjoy it for a while on their own, but I’m not sure how long that will last.'" The Steelers have French ties, too. Maguire discussed them in his article on the topic. "The Steelers can claim a connection to France, as well. 'Pittsburgh bears the mark of Franco-American history: in the 18th century, the French built Fort Duquesne there, on the territory that would become the future city,' said the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs in a social media post this week." Oct 11, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints tight end Juwan Johnson (83) runs against Minnesota Vikings outside linebacker Andrew van Ginkel (43) during the second half at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The title of America's Team already exists. The Dallas Cowboys hold that title, even though the 1970's nickname lacks relevance in modern day. The Cowboys haven't won enough to command that kind of attention. The title of France's Team may be on the line on Sunday. Whether or not the two teams can generate enough interest in American football is still to be seen. France is a country that takes pride in what Americans call soccer. Still, the game is an interesting opportunity for the Saints to celebrate their French roots. They will hope to head home with a win.

item.title: Rangers add veteran forward amid hot start to 2026-27
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Rangers add veteran forward amid hot start to 2026-27 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Rangers are one of the most surprising teams in the NHL through the early part of the season as they are in second place in the Metropolitan Division, just two points behind the Stanley Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes. In an effort to improve the overall depth of their forward group, the Rangers have signed Luke Glendening after the 13-year NHL veteran had a professional try out with the team. Glendening has played center at many points in his career, but he can also play on the wing. The 37-year-old has primarily been a defensive player throughout his career. He has never scored more than 12 goals in a season. He has not scored in double figures since the 2018-19 season when he scored 10 goals while playing for the Detroit Red Wings. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Glendening spent 10 years with the Red Wings, two years with the Tampa Bay Lightning, two years with the Dallas Stars along with single seasons with the New Jersey Devils and Philadelphia Flyers. Glendening is knowns for his speed on the ice as well as his ability in the face-off circle. He has connected on 55.6 percent of the draws he has taken throughout his career. The Rangers will likely use him on their fourth line and as a penalty killer. His speed on the ice allows him to cover much of the defensive zone when his team is shorthanded. The Rangers have had an issue with their fourth-line center since veteran Joe Veleno went down with a lower-body injury. Glendening will have an excellent chance to fill that role.

item.title: Knicks superfans give baby ultimate name in honor of team's NBA championship win
item.description: Knicks superfans give baby ultimate name in honor of team's NBA championship win originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . This New York Knicks couple went above and beyond to celebrate the team's NBA championship win by naming their newborn son after the historic event. When the Knicks clinched the title, Yvonne Gonzalez-Bradford was seven months pregnant, and she and her husband Vance Bradford already had names picked out for their bundle of joy. The couple decided on Lady Victoria if the baby was a girl, and Prestige Wisdom if the baby was a boy. The city came alive after the Knicks won over the San Antonio Spurs in five games of the seven-game series, where there was nowhere in New York you couldn't hear ecstatic fans cheering, "Knicks in 5!" Vance told Today.com that it sparked an idea to potentially change the name of their son as he asked his wife, “What if we give our son a name for a champion? What about Knickson?’” Yvonne was on board, and Vance revealed that the name would be special not only to honor the Knicks winning the championship but because his family has been die-hard fans for years. Two days later, Yvonne suggested Fyve as a middle name to reference the number of games that the Knicks won to bring home the title. “You know how when something happens so well in your favor, you don’t want to jinx it?” Vance says, recounting how excited he was to hear his wife's suggestion. “I was just like, ‘Yep! Absolutely. That’s it!’” Vance added another layer to his son's name sharing, “The Roman numeral for five is ‘V,’ like my name, so he’s named after me in a way. Five is also an indivisible number. So he’s our indivisible champion. You can hear him cooing in the background right now.” Knickson Fyve was born on August 8, 2026, which is also significant to his mother, as he was welcomed into the world on Yvonne's birthday. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Yvonne Gonzalez (@ygb.nyc) The couple has already been asked what will happen if Knickson decides to be a fan of another NBA team in the future. “If he turns out to be a Celtics fan or a Sixers fan, again he’s still Knickson Bradford, who is in the boardroom,” Vance humorously says. "We wanted to have a very strong and firm name that would lead to a cool life. Knickson Fyve is definitely our motto. Knickson Fyve forever!” The Knicks just finished their first regular-season game against the Philadelphia 76ers on Oct. 20. Before tip-off, the banner was raised to showcase their championship win as well as be awarded with their rings. Unfortunately for the reigning NBA champions, they lost their home opener 100-106, but there is still more than enough time to get right back in rhythm. The next game for the Knicks will be against the Boston Celtics on Friday, Oct. 23 at 7 p.m. ET. The second person who supported Haliburton more than any non-family member during his rehab was at the game in reality. Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray, who spent much of 2025 recovering from a torn achilles himself, became an important confidant for the Pacers star guard. item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
